BUS516 — Abkr.
Abkr sir is a very good faculty member and teaches really well. His classes can feel a bit boring sometimes, but if you follow the classes properly, a large portion of your studies will already be covered. While teaching, sir clearly mentions which topics are important for short questions, which are important for short notes, and so on. If you follow those before the exam, it becomes much easier.
The quizzes are MCQ-based. He takes 3 quizzes, and the best 2 are counted. You have to study from the textbook.
In Midterm 1, Midterm 2, and the Final Exam, he gives questions in three written formats. First, there are short notes. For these, writing the definition of the topic along with an example in 2–3 lines is enough to get good marks. Then there are broad questions, where you should write in some detail. Sir usually mentions the important topics beforehand, and the questions mostly come from those areas. He becomes happy if you write answers from the textbook.
After that comes the Management Decision Problem section. There is usually a short case study for this part. You need to read the case, understand the core concept, and explain how, as a manager, you would solve the problem.
Sir gives marks quite generously. There is also one group report, and he is very serious about it. Your combined plagiarism and AI usage must not exceed 20%; otherwise, sir will give a zero. The report also needs to be accurate and error-free. If you do it properly, you can achieve a very good grade. Otherwise, your grade may be badly affected.
He is not very strict about presentations. However, you must attend classes regularly if you want full marks in attendance. The grading is fair, and the curve depends on the overall class performance.
